title: 25 FOR REASONS
subtitle: A college-football poll with receipts.
question: If everybody played next Saturday, which 25 teams would we believe in most?

cadence.sunday: Proof, complication, or death markers on every live claim.
cadence.tuesday: The new 25, full reasons, movement ledger, and one published dissent.
cadence.thursday: Three games capable of changing the board.
cadence.saturday: A quiet watch order built for one good window, not an endless feed.

sources.label: 2026 preseason FPI board and roster notes

teams.reason: The highest quarterback–receiver ceiling in the sport, carrying the season’s nastiest road schedule.
teams.case: Julian Sayin and Jeremiah Smith make every snap expandable; the roster still has national-title depth.
teams.doubt: The defense has real holes, and road trips to Texas, Indiana, Iowa, Nebraska, and USC leave no soft month.
teams.proof: Win an early road game without asking the passing game to be perfect.

teams.reason: Unusual defensive continuity and fewer imaginary preseason dependencies than anyone else.
teams.case: CJ Carr leads a talented offense while nine of the ten leading tacklers return.
teams.doubt: The two-back engine is gone, and the playoff path now begins with championship expectations.
teams.proof: Show that the new run game can finish drives instead of merely protecting the defense.

teams.reason: The Arch Manning window is now; the unresolved run game keeps this from being No. 1.
teams.case: Manning finished 2025 as an efficient, dangerous passer with another elite skill group around him.
teams.doubt: A contender this expensive cannot keep treating ordinary rushing success as an optional feature.
teams.proof: Control one serious opponent on the ground when the box knows what is coming.

teams.reason: Dante Moore, deep talent, championship capacity—and two new coordinators to assimilate.
teams.case: The quarterback and blue-chip skill core survived another playoff run.
teams.doubt: Coordinator turnover can turn a complete roster into a September installation project.
teams.proof: Look like the same adult operation before the conference schedule becomes cruel.

teams.reason: Back-to-back SEC champions receive institutional trust until the rebuilt secondary spends it.
teams.case: Gunner Stockton, Nate Frazier, and the sport’s most reliable contender infrastructure return.
teams.doubt: New defensive backs meet road tests at Alabama and Ole Miss before they can hide.
teams.proof: Survive one explosive passing offense without retreating into conservative coverage.

teams.reason: The undefeated champion deserves deference; repeating after turnover would change the sport permanently.
teams.case: Curt Cignetti just produced a 16–0 champion and added a 31-game starting quarterback in Josh Hoover.
teams.doubt: The exact continuity that made Indiana feel older than everybody else has been broken up.
teams.proof: Run the same calm, grown-up offense with different people in the most important chairs.

teams.reason: A national finalist plus Darian Mensah creates an immediate return path; the defensive reconstruction is real.
teams.case: Mensah joins Mark Fletcher and Malachi Toney in an offense with title-game memory.
teams.doubt: The defensive front seven lost too many answers to assume another January run.
teams.proof: Create pressure without selling out the secondary.

teams.reason: Lane Kiffin, Sam Leavitt, and the leading transfer class: enormous ceiling, delicious combustion potential.
teams.case: The new quarterback and receiver room can become the country’s fastest offensive installation.
teams.doubt: A roster assembled at speed still has to become a team while the SEC watches.
teams.proof: Win a game that requires patience rather than a track meet.

teams.reason: The Big 12 champion has a serious floor; quarterback health determines whether the ceiling survives.
teams.case: The run game and recent championship evidence make the Red Raiders the league’s adult.
teams.doubt: Will Hammond returns from an ACL injury while the defense replaces its loudest playmakers.
teams.proof: Let Hammond be efficient without turning every drive into a medical suspense film.

teams.reason: Five returning blockers, a huge recruiting class, and Gary Patterson. The excuse inventory is empty.
teams.case: Jayden Maiava finally gets continuity in front of him while the defense gains an adult architect.
teams.doubt: USC has been winning the offseason longer than it has been winning important November games.
teams.proof: Tackle well and close a one-score conference game without theater.

teams.reason: This is no longer a brand ranking. It is a referendum on whether Alabama can become physically frightening again.
teams.case: Kalen DeBoer has won 20 games in two seasons and still recruits like Alabama.
teams.doubt: The quarterback changes, the 2025 run game ranked near the bottom of FBS, and Indiana exposed the distance.
teams.proof: Move a good defensive front when everybody in the stadium expects run.

teams.reason: Matt Campbell and 39 transfers: either an intelligently assembled machine or a very expensive group project.
teams.case: Rocco Becht brings 26 starts, Carson Hansen brings production, and Campbell knows how to organize scarcity.
teams.doubt: The number 39 is also a warning about shared language, role clarity, and September chemistry.
teams.proof: Look connected on third down before talent can cover the seams.

teams.reason: Eleven straight wins proved the shape; the ending proved the fragility.
teams.case: Marcel Reed returns to an offense that already knows it can sustain a serious run.
teams.doubt: Both lines lost answers, the schedule stiffens, and Reed still owes the ball better care.
teams.proof: Finish a close game after the first plan stops working.

teams.reason: A championship defense being asked to carry an offense that must finally become ordinary-good.
teams.case: Brent Venables can build a suffocating defense with replacement parts.
teams.doubt: John Mateer, the line, and the run game all need improvement at the same time.
teams.proof: Create four reliable yards without requiring quarterback improvisation.

teams.reason: Kyle Whittingham plus Bryce Underwood is the season’s strangest and most compelling culture experiment.
teams.case: A veteran defensive program-builder inherits a rare quarterback and a roster built for contact.
teams.doubt: A new sideline does not instantly erase the program’s recent on- and off-field instability.
teams.proof: Give Underwood a coherent game rather than a weekly rescue assignment.

teams.reason: Consecutive 11-win seasons are evidence, not atmosphere.
teams.case: Bear Bachmeier and LJ Martin return to the league’s preseason favorite.
teams.doubt: New defensive leadership has to preserve the thing that made the last two seasons travel.
teams.proof: Win when the offense is merely normal.

teams.reason: Enough offensive continuity to matter; an entire post-Kiffin identity still to invent.
teams.case: Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy give Pete Golding two honest offensive anchors.
teams.doubt: The staff and defense changed around them, and every close call becomes a referendum on the succession.
teams.proof: Show an offensive identity that is not a tribute act.

teams.reason: Jim Knowles can make the defense serious immediately. Nobody has earned certainty at quarterback.
teams.case: A more disciplined defense can keep the season alive while the offense chooses its operator.
teams.doubt: George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon enter without the experience a contender normally buys.
teams.proof: Produce boring, repeatable quarterback decisions for four quarters.

teams.reason: Potentially exceptional receivers, a new quarterback, and the clearest Dabo inflection point yet.
teams.case: Chad Morris returns to an offense that can put Christopher Vizzina inside an unusually good receiver room.
teams.doubt: A 7–6 season made “the old Clemson” an argument instead of a baseline.
teams.proof: Turn receiver talent into explosive points before the crowd starts remembering 2018.

teams.reason: Can the infrastructure survive the end of the Whittingham era? We believe it can—barely.
teams.case: Years of developmental competence remain in the building even after the defining coach leaves.
teams.doubt: Institutional memory is not play-calling, recruiting, or fourth-quarter authority.
teams.proof: Look unmistakably like Utah after the person most associated with “Utah football” is gone.

teams.reason: Quietly respected by models and preseason consensus; a perfect early candidate for “we noticed first.”
teams.case: The underlying roster and returning structure grade better than the national conversation.
teams.doubt: Big Ten travel turns respectable depth into a weekly stress test.
teams.proof: Carry offensive efficiency across one cross-country conference trip.

teams.reason: Jon Sumrall inherits real talent and an SEC-sized proof requirement.
teams.case: The receiver room gives the new staff enough speed to make the reset visible quickly.
teams.doubt: Talent at key positions is not the same thing as a complete line-to-line football team.
teams.proof: Beat a good opponent without making the new-coach story the entire offense.

teams.reason: LaNorris Sellers is the reason; whether anybody can protect him is the entire ranking.
teams.case: Sellers returned with the talent to make Kendal Briles’ reset immediately dangerous.
teams.doubt: The 2025 line was disastrous, and quarterback brilliance cannot be the pass-protection plan.
teams.proof: Let a deep concept develop without asking Sellers to escape first.

teams.reason: The outsider benchmark: the team that reveals whether this poll actually watches beyond the power brands.
teams.case: Boise remains the cleanest preseason proxy for the strongest program outside the Power Four.
teams.doubt: The new Pac-12 carries opportunity and a weekly credibility tax.
teams.proof: Beat the kind of opponent whose logo normally wins the argument before kickoff.

teams.reason: An elite imported runner, institutional defensive competence, and the possibility of extremely strange winning.
teams.case: LJ Phillips arrives after 1,920 rushing yards at South Dakota, attached to Iowa’s usual floor.
teams.doubt: A new quarterback and a wave of new starters can turn “usual floor” into nostalgia.
teams.proof: Score enough early that the punter does not become the offensive identity again.
